anomalies.observed: In the WATER LEVEL / Safety Switches block, R6 (10 k) is tied between +3V3 and the FLOAT_HIGH net (with C5 100 n to GND on the same net), and R9 (10 k) is tied between the FLOAT_LOW net and GND. J1 pin 2 (HIGH) drives FLOAT_HIGH and pin 3 (LOW) drives FLOAT_LOW.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification's reference connectivity, R6 is the pull-up on FLOAT_LOW and R9 is the pull-down on FLOAT_HIGH ('R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k'). The two 10 k pull resistors are assigned to the opposite nets in the drawing.

evidence.quote: R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k (OPNhydro_r2.cir, §4.4)
Safety Switches: R6 10k from +3V3+3V3 to the upper net labelled FLOAT_HIGH (C5 100n to GND); R9 10k from the lower net labelled FLOAT_LOW to GND (WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES block)

anomalies.impact: The idle/fail bias of the two float safety inputs is inverted relative to the intended design. The low-level pump-cutoff interlock (R2 from FLOAT_LOW into T1 base) and the high-level overflow interlock (R11 from FLOAT_HIGH into T4 base) therefore see the wrong default levels: with the float switches referenced as in the reference, FLOAT_LOW would sit low by default (pull-down) keeping the main circulation pump disabled, and FLOAT_HIGH would sit high by default (pull-up) keeping the ATO valve closed, defeating the ATO fill and the safety cutoffs.

parsed.summary: The power train, isolators, TMC2209 drivers (110 m sense, 14k/10k7 VREF dividers, unique UART addresses), buck/LDO feedback and the DNP/unwired items all match the specification; the only deviation from the documented reference connectivity is that the float pull resistors R6 and R9 are on the wrong nets (R6 pull-up on FLOAT_HIGH and R9 pull-down on FLOAT_LOW, instead of R6 on FLOAT_LOW and R9 on FLOAT_HIGH), which inverts the safety-interlock idle states.
